item.title: [paper] A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
item.description: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control.

item.title: [paper] Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
item.description: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability.

item.title: [paper] Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
item.description: This survey unifies video understanding and generation through world modeling, organizing progress around inferring, synthesizing, sharing, and interacting with latent temporal states to emphasize persistent dynamics over clip-level perception.

item.title: [paper] Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
item.description: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution.

item.title: [paper] Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
item.description: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations.

item.title: [paper] Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
item.description: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision.

item.title: [paper] SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
item.description: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images.

item.title: [paper] Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
item.description: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage.

item.title: [paper] METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories.

item.title: [paper] BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
item.description: BrickWright improves physical validity of AI-generated LEGO assemblies by providing agents with an assembly API and feasibility validator, achieving perfect validity while preserving prompt adherence.

item.title: [paper] EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
item.description: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true.

item.title: [paper] Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
item.description: Single-image 3D generation has achieved high fidelity on curated benchmarks, yet degrades sharply on real-world images with uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions.

item.title: [paper] Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
item.description: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing.

item.title: [paper] OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
item.description: Monocular models recover 3D geometry from a single image in one pass, but most assume a pinhole camera and produce distorted geometry on the wide-angle imagery produced by fisheye and panoramic lenses.

item.title: [paper] GigaBench: Benchmarking Learnable Representations for Gigapixel Image Compression and Super-Resolution
item.description: Learnable Representations (LRs) can fit parametric families of functions to diverse kinds of signals.

item.title: [paper] A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
item.description: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero.

item.title: [paper] UniVOE: A Removal-Driven Framework for Interaction-Aware Universal Video Object Editing
item.description: Video object removal and injection are reciprocal editing operations between object-present and object-absent video states, yet they differ substantially in training difficulty.

item.title: [paper] WorldForge V2: Eliciting Camera-Trajectory Alignment in Video Diffusion Models
item.description: Video diffusion models have learned rich 3D/4D priors, making them promising for scene generation and video re-rendering.

item.title: [paper] Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
item.description: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer.

item.title: [paper] Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
item.description: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated.

item.title: [paper] HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
item.description: Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks.

item.title: [paper] BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
item.description: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly.

item.title: [news] Deploy AI in a HIPAA-eligible environment with Amazon Quick
item.description: Amazon Quick is a HIPAA-eligible service, but eligibility is not the same as compliance.

item.title: [news] Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: Voice agents often wait for an agent's full response before starting speech synthesis, adding latency users feel directly.

item.title: [paper] Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
item.description: Instrumental convergence is often invoked as a general reason to expect capable agents to acquire or express power-seeking subgoals: self-preservation, resource acquisition, deception, or resistance to oversight which poses an important threat to the society.

item.title: [paper] F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
item.description: F2G-Pose is a real-time feed-forward framework that predicts category-level object pose, metric size, and completed shape from a single RGB-D image using dense visual features, DGCNN tokenization, and a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer.

item.title: [paper] Bilingual Language Models Capture Cross-Linguistic Influence in Second-Language Reading
item.description: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1).

item.title: [paper] OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation
item.description: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation.

item.title: [paper] Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy
item.description: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $μ$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $μ$ with total-variation error $α$.

item.title: [paper] How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
item.description: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage.

item.title: [paper] SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
item.description: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood.

item.title: [paper] CRANE: Post-Hoc Counterfactual Retrieval for Multimodal Classifiers
item.description: Counterfactual explanation methods have been introduced for unimodal settings, with dedicated frameworks for tabular, timeseries, text, and image data, yet no post-hoc method has been designed for classifiers that learn from multimodal inputs.

item.title: [paper] Simulated Control Evals
item.description: Control evaluations measure whether safeguards can prevent an AI model from causing undesired outcomes even when it is intentionally trying to do so. These evaluations typically use purpose-built control settings and extrapolate their results to a model's deployment.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Best-of-$k$: Prior-Consistent DAPS for Ambiguous Nonlinear Inverse Problems
item.description: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous.

item.title: [paper] VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
item.description: Institutions that deploy large language models in regulated settings often need technical evidence of responsible AI practices before approving a deployment.

item.title: [paper] Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
item.description: Accuracy on medical examinations is common evidence offered for the clinical use of language models, yet a health system that intends to run an open model on its own hardware needs to know considerably more: whether the model recognizes when it is likely to be wrong, whether…

item.title: [paper] Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
item.description: Understanding and controlling how systems evolve is central to science and engineering, where many problems require reasoning about complete trajectories.

item.title: [paper] Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
item.description: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear. We ask the reverse question: when an LLM is confident, consistent, and wrong, do users bend towards it?

item.title: [paper] What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
item.description: Optimized unmasking policies for masked diffusion language models improve efficiency by using trajectory-contraction targets with confidence and hidden states, achieving better speed-accuracy trade-offs with minimal overhead.

item.title: [paper] Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
item.description: Test-time regression provides a learnable, closed-form alternative to pooling for compressing sequences in efficient language and multimodal models.

item.title: [paper] Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure
item.description: In the post-API landscape, social-media profiling has become inexpensive and automated: Large Language Models (LLMs) can extract structured information from unstructured content and deduce attributes users never disclosed.

item.title: [paper] On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
item.description: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts.

item.title: [paper] CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
item.description: Large language models have shown outstanding performance on text-first tasks such as coding, math, and writing.

item.title: [paper] Squaring-the-Sphere: Distortion-Free and Seamless Panorama Generation via CubeAtlas
item.description: Generating 360-degree panoramas requires both local perspective fidelity and global spherical continuity.

item.title: [paper] When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation
item.description: Online Policy Distillation (OPD) often outperforms offline methods such as Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) by training on trajectories sampled directly from the student.

item.title: [paper] Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
item.description: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup.

item.title: [paper] Contestable Agents for Data Governance: Recording Human Stewardship of AI-Generated Metadata Across Structured and Unstructured Systems
item.description: Industrial organizations hold operational knowledge in structured records, such as telemetry, point lists, and transactions, and in unstructured sources, such as manuals, service notes, communications, and inspection reports.

item.title: [paper] Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
item.description: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL).

item.title: [paper] Shift-aware score transport for privacy auditing without retraining
item.description: Privacy auditing empirically assesses privacy leakage by using membership inference attacks to establish lower bounds on privacy loss.

item.title: [paper] Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Agentic reinforcement learning rewards a complete episode, yet the policy needs credit for every decision inside it.

item.title: [paper] PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
item.description: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families.

item.title: [paper] LACToS: Local Anomaly Detection via Conditional Typicality of Superpixels
item.description: Local anomaly detection is the task of identifying spatially confined anomalous or out-of-distribution (OOD) regions within an otherwise in-distribution (ID) image.

item.title: [paper] An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
item.description: Knowledge graph-to-text (KG-to-text) generation verbalizes a set of knowledge graph triples into fluent natural language. While fine-tuned encoder-decoder models have long been the standard approach, recent LLMs are becoming increasingly competitive.

item.title: [paper] Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
item.description: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training.

item.title: [paper] Nonparametric autoregressive estimation of probability distributions with parallel gradient boosting
item.description: Nonparametric estimation of joint probability distributions is a core problem in statistics, which is notoriously challenging with high-dimensional data.

item.title: [paper] Diffusion-Based Synthesis of Complete 3D Biparametric Prostate MRI
item.description: Synthetic biparametric MRI (bpMRI) may help alleviate the limited availability of large and representative prostate MRI datasets for deep learning applications.

item.title: [paper] Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
item.description: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates.

item.title: [paper] Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
item.description: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces.

item.title: [paper] The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
item.description: Metaphor is a crucial aspect of human cognition. As such, we would like to understand how it is represented in large language models (LLMs) and how it might be controlled.

item.title: [paper] From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals.

item.title: [news] Stop guessing auto scaling targets for TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: Teams deploying custom text-to-speech models on Amazon SageMaker AI often guess at autoscaling thresholds, and a wrong guess either wastes GPU spend or breaches a latency SLO.

item.title: [paper] Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural
item.description: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction.

item.title: [paper] DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
item.description: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget.

item.title: [paper] Piano2Pop: Expanding Piano Demos into Pop Productions Without Aligned Supervision
item.description: We introduce Piano2Pop, a music-expansion task that transforms piano MIDI into instrumental pop productions.

item.title: [news] How Rescale built an AI triage agent with Strands Agents and AI-DLC
item.description: Rescale used the AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) framework on AWS, with Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock, to build an intelligent test-triage agent in weeks.

item.title: [paper] FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation
item.description: Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations.

item.title: [paper] Evaluation of Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Software Ensembles for Hippocampal Segmentation
item.description: Accurate hippocampal segmentation can be a useful tool for diagnosing and monitoring neurological conditions such as Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy. While numerous automated segmentation methods exist, their clinical adoption remains limited.

item.title: [paper] Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
item.description: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX).

item.title: [paper] SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
item.description: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive.

item.title: [paper] AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
item.description: AgentVQA is an offline benchmark assessing vision-language models on realistic agentic tasks across web, robotics, video, games, and spatial planning, revealing that visual grounding and state tracking errors are the primary failure modes.

item.title: [paper] Self-Supervised Multibeam Sonar Restoration via Coherent Forward Modeling
item.description: Multibeam imaging sonar produces intensity images degraded by coherent speckle and system-induced blur, while clean reflectivity targets are rarely available.

item.title: [paper] Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
item.description: As LLM agents operate over corpora of more than ten thousand tools, selecting the right tool for a complex multi-step user instruction becomes a central bottleneck.

item.title: [paper] Evaluating the Applicability of LLM Inference Optimizations on Apple Silicon
item.description: Apple Silicon is among the most widely used platforms for local LLM inference, yet nearly all inference optimizations are designed and validated on server-class NVIDIA GPUs under batched serving workloads.

item.title: [paper] MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models
item.description: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong potential for video anomaly detection, but dense frame-level inference makes them impractical for real-time deployment.

item.title: [news] Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
item.description: Flint-interactive gives AI agents a language for creating interactive visualizations. Click a chart, filter data, highlight related content, and explore beyond the view the author originally chose.

item.title: [paper] Ask About the Right Moment: Training-Free Object Identity Reasoning for Video-Language Models
item.description: Many questions about a video concern one physical object. Where does the ball end up after the cups are shuffled? Which card is the queen? How often was the mug covered?

item.title: [paper] Measuring the Verifier's Floor: How Much Apparent Rare-Word Text-to-Speech Error Is ASR Error?
item.description: Text-to-speech (TTS) is usually evaluated by transcribing its output with an automatic speech recognition (ASR) system, so the word error rate also counts recognizer errors. We measure these errors on human recordings of the test sentences.

item.title: [paper] From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
item.description: As wearable and digital health systems increasingly generate longitudinal physiological records, communicating these observations in patient-accessible language remains a significant challenge.

item.title: [paper] AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
item.description: AnyGameRenderer is a video-to-video generative model that transforms low-quality agent-built game footage into high-fidelity visuals while preserving layout, camera, and entity timing.

item.title: [paper] RheOPT: Few-Shot Non-Newtonian Flow Prediction via Newtonian Pretraining of RheOFormer
item.description: Despite advances in numerical methods, non-Newtonian flow simulations remain computationally expensive because velocity and stress must be advanced together through rate- and history-dependent constitutive dynamics.

item.title: [paper] Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
item.description: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units. Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution.

item.title: [paper] How Different, or Different How? Stance Granularity in Viewpoint Selection for Dialog Systems that Engage Users with Alternative Views
item.description: Systems that aim to help a user engage with viewpoints other than their own have to decide how different those viewpoints should be. Viewpoints are mainly represented on a scalar scale, too coarse to distinguish viewpoints that disagree with the user about different things.

item.title: [paper] MixPT: Point Transformer with Interleaved Window and Global Attention
item.description: Point cloud transformers aim to capture detailed local geometry and relationships across a scene at a manageable computational cost. Two common approaches are window attention and global attention.
